scalars.scalar_value: This is a full-time career appointment, exempt from overtime pay (monthly paid). The Chief Communications Officer position is appointed by and serves at the discretion of the Laboratory Director, and this appointment is at will and may be terminated at any time with or without cause.
Experience leading communications activities in a DOE national laboratory or FFRDC environment.

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic communications, public affairs, or related fields, ideally within a science-driven, research, academic, government, or similarly complex institutional environment.

items.item_text: This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
This position requires daily on-site presence at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA, with occasional business travel.
Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.
Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic communications, public affairs, or related fields, ideally within a science-driven, research, academic, government, or similarly complex institutional environment.
Experience leading communications activities in a DOE national laboratory or FFRDC environment.
Significant experience leading crisis and emergency communications, operating effectively under pressure while maintaining transparency and alignment with institutional values.
Experience driving organizational alignment, cross-functional collaboration, and institutional change in complex environments.
Leadership & Institutional Strategy

Develop and execute an enterprise-wide communications strategy aligned with the Laboratory’s scientific mission, strategic priorities, and reputation, with clear outcomes and data analytics to evaluate progress, including the impacts of AI on stakeholder information gathering.
Advise the Laboratory Director and executive leadership on reputation, issues management, stakeholder engagement, and institutional positioning.
Translate long-term institutional vision into actionable communication strategies that advance scientific leadership and programmatic ambitions across internal and external audiences.
Drive integrated storytelling across programs and directorates to reinforce a unified Laboratory identity.
Science Communication & Impact
Position the Laboratory as a global leader in science, innovation, and impact.
Lead communications across the Lab’s research portfolio in energy, computation, artificial intelligence, quantum, materials, biological sciences, and related disciplines.
Proactively engage national and global media to elevate the Laboratory’s reputation for scientific excellence and impact.
Connect programmatic priorities to broader societal challenges to strengthen understanding of federally funded science and its value.
Direct a modern digital and media ecosystem aligned with audience expectations and institutional storytelling needs.
Internal Communications, Culture & Engagement
Lead a Lab-wide internal communications program that fosters shared purpose across a complex organization with multiple internal communities.
Partner with Lab leaders to communicate a culture grounded in stewardship, shared values, and safety.
Work with functional areas (e.g., the Stewardship Office and Human Resources) to communicate organizational change in ways that build trust and engagement.
Strengthen cohesion across research and operations communications teams to support execution of Laboratory priorities.
Lead internal efforts to execute programs that foster employee engagement.
Crisis & Emergency Communications
Prepare for and lead emergency and crisis communications that protect people, assets and reputation while maintaining and building stakeholder trust.
Advise senior leadership in real time during high-consequence crises, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and institutional credibility.
Be available after hours and on weekends to advise and lead crisis communications as needed.
Stakeholder Engagement & Relationship Building
Build trust and alignment across stakeholder communities through clear, consistent, and responsive messaging.
Serve as the senior communications interface with DOE, UC,, the State of California, academic partners, industry, and local communities.
Coordinate communications across national laboratory peers (the National Laboratories Chief Communications Officers) and research partners to reinforce mission alignment and collective impact.
Represent the Laboratory in national forums where communications, science policy, and institutional reputation converge.
Organizational Leadership & Team Development
Strengthen integration across decentralized communications teams to lead a cohesive, Lab-wide communications enterprise, leveraging distributed expertise into a unified strategic function.
Foster a high-performing communications culture grounded in collaboration, trust, accountability, innovation, and excellence.
Oversee budgeting, workforce planning, and resource allocation for Strategic Communications, aligned with institutional priorities.
Anticipate and adapt to shifts in the information landscape, including misinformation, evolving practices, and AI-enabled tools and workflows.
Strategic Communications Leadership
Familiarity with data-informed communications approaches and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools and workflows.
Record of advising senior executives on reputation, issues management, and strategic messaging.
Stakeholder Relationships
Crisis, Risk & Reputation Management
Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness
Proven success in leading and developing high-performing, multidisciplinary teams.

Proven ability to design and execute enterprise-scale, integrated communications strategies aligned with institutional mission, scientific leadership, and long-term programmatic priorities in large, distributed organizations.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with deep fluency in modern practices across digital, media, internal communications, branding, and executive messaging.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across complex stakeholder ecosystems, including federal agencies, academic partners, and public-sector institutions.
Ability to balance diverse and sometimes competing stakeholder needs while maintaining institutional coherence and credibility.
High emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and credibility at all levels, with the ability to influence without authority and build trust across scientific, operational, and executive communities.
Proven ability to protect institutional reputation while sustaining trust with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong budgeting, operational planning, and resource management skills.
